title: Subway Violin
premise: A long drama of violin music in a subway concourse. Violinist Suwan and apprentice Shuanger guard the old violin Nightingale; Shuanger and Axi look nearly alike but wear different sleeve bands; the folding violin-case cart is crushed and must be avoided; repertoire notebook, count memory, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_performer: A woman violinist in her thirties, black beret, black performance coat, violin in left hand and bow in right, focused expression.

segments.action: At dusk, violinist Suwan enters the subway concourse and takes the Nightingale violin from its velvet bag to tune.
Five emergency lights glow under the concourse beam; Suwan looks up to confirm they will not glare on the violin face.
Two signal bells hang by the gates; before a train arrives they chime briefly, and Suwan stops the bow to let the sound pass.
Suwan sets the Nightingale violin on her shoulder; the first melody echoes along the ad pillars.
Suwan unties the ribbon, opens the repertoire notebook, and writes the rush-hour set beside the subway map.
She glances at the five emergency lights under the beam, then clips the permit copy back into the repertoire notebook.
Suwan closes the repertoire notebook, sets the Nightingale violin back on its pad, and waits for the next train's noise to pass.
At the dawn platform edge, Suwan greets young Shuanger pushing the folding violin-case cart; screen doors mirror both shadows.

segments.action: Months later on a leak night, Suwan packs the violin spot alone in the subway concourse; the Nightingale violin leans by a pillar.
Condensate from the ceiling drips into the repertoire notebook; map corners curl and set-list ink bleeds in the damp.

segments.action: The performance season stretches on; every day Suwan finds gaps between announcements to play in the subway concourse.
In the morning rush she softens the tone as commuters stream past.
At high summer noon, AC drips in the concourse; Suwan wipes fine mist from the top plate.
Through autumn rain, pillar ads rotate three times; the Nightingale violin still hangs on her shoulder.
After the last New Year's Eve train, Suwan alone finishes one more piece facing the empty concourse.
At dawn, Suwan patrols the platform edge; the folding violin-case cart sits outside the yellow line, wheel lock tight.
She crouches to check the folding violin-case cart handle, hinge, and small wheels, ducking a gust from an arriving train.
Suwan returns to the concourse violin spot and confirms those three rosin cakes are still in the paper box.
Staff push a yellow-plate luggage cart across the platform, bed open, no nightingale sticker at all.
Rush hour blacks out suddenly; crowds pack the platform edge; signs above the screen doors flicker.
Suwan backs up guarding the Nightingale violin; a corner hits a metal bench and a thin crack opens in the top plate.

The station supervisor points at the cleaning cart and warns her to yield; Suwan holds the patched Nightingale violin steadier.

segments.action: From the transfer corridor comes flower-seller Xiaoyu; under a light-brown scarf her profile at a glance looks like young Shuanger.
When Xiaoyu offers flowers her wireless in-ear shows; Suwan only asks her to avoid the crowd by the violin spot.
At dusk years later, Suwan with a bandaged right wrist alone enters the sealed abandoned platform.
